newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE FRENCH FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE FRENCH FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the French first division:

Cannes welcome back midfielder Cedric Daury, who was suspended last week, for a tricky tie against Lille. The team from northern France have been one of the surprises of the early season and want to avenge their 4-1 trouncing by Monaco against another team from the French Riviera.
Guingamp will miss injured goalkeeper Angelo Hugues. Metz are without captain Sylvain Kastendeuch, who sustained a calf injury in the UEFA Cup against Sporting Lisbon.

Champions Auxerre, outclassed by Grasshopper Zurich in the European Champions' League on Wednesday, face another tricky match at Le Havre. Defender Franck Ranarivony may be back from suspension but coach Guy Roux is still without central defender Franck Silvestre and striker Lilian Lalandes, though both are likely to return next week.

Morale is high in Lens after two consecutive victories as they entertain lowly Nice. Key defender Thomas Sikora and Cameroon striker Marc Vivien Foe return for Lens. Nice welcome back marksman Mohammed Chaouch.

Despite being depleted by injuries -- playmaker Franck Gava is the most notable absentee -- Lyon hope the replacement of coach Guy Stephan by former French international Bernard Lacombe will spur them to victory against Rennes. Rennes are without suspended Stephane Guivarc'h, the league's leading scorer.

On a high after winning six matches in a row to come back to within three points of leaders Paris St Germain, Monaco were brought back to earth in the UEFA Cup with a 1-0 home defeat by Borussia Moenchengladbach. Coach Jean Tigana knows he must beware of Bordeaux, the team for whom he played for most his career, even though they have not won in the principality for 15 years. Bordeaux, coached by Tigana's childhood friend Rolland Courbis, had not won for six matches before beating Montpellier 3-1 last week.

Booed by their fans after losing 1-0 at home to Nantes last week, Marseille hope the return of captain Jean-Philippe Durand will help them win at last at lowly Montpellier. The absence through injury of half a dozen Montpellier players may help the former European champions.
Nancy and Caen, both promoted from the second division this season, have been struggling. Defeat would be very costly for both. Caen are without regular goalkeeper Luc Borrelli.

Nantes solved their problems on the pitch with a fine 1-0 victory at Marseille last week but have been shaken off it with the resignation of club president Guy Scherrer. On current form, they look capable of beating gifted Strasbourg, who welcome Czeck Jan Suchoparek back from injury but will miss defender Francis Llacer.

After a bad run which saw them lose for the first time this season in the league at Rennes and crash at Galatasaray 4-2 in the Cup Winners' Cup, leaders Paris St Germain set all doubts aside by crushing the Turks 4-0 on Thursday. Ricardo can rely on a full squad against the Corsicans, who will field key striker Anton Drobnjak for one of his last games before he moves to Italy's Perugia.
